scope: Only role reports/checkpoint; all code, source dossiers, world packs, canonical plan/RUN, private saves and library remain read-only.

baseline.head: 97c28efece4fd6248b6f075ad0c6927c3d0432df
baseline.drift_resolution: Reread changed planning/strategy scope and own RUN/approval. The added integration-strategy role consumes aspect findings and has no runtime writer authority. Human-review hold and this role's report-only scope remain unchanged. Updated the source-to-feature evidence range after line movement.
baseline.qualification: Fingerprints identify inspected revisions; long files were read by named ranges/searches, not claimed fully reviewed.

measurements.qualification: No gameplay or import/build execution; no cost or savings inferred from reports, counts or static complexity.

findings.title: Link complete effect and native-consumer closure before labelling content integrated

evidence.claim: Nested reference traversal checks energy/event/site/situation/pursuit; it does not close source/power/spawn/native catalogue bindings.
Capability-source and executable-power acquisition resolve their definitions during execution.
An encoded item key is validated for JSON shape and quality, not actual item reconstruction.
Native publication resolves actual actors/items/skills and milestone unlock adapters.
Actual native quest/flag/availability entries must exist.
The host already stages native publication and checks future committed rewards; retain this boundary.

findings.current_player_behavior: Existing registered work can produce actual kits and XP through guarded native publication. A detached definition can pass registry shape validation while still lacking a referenced source, native item/unlock, or usable consumer; this is not player-accessible delivery.
findings.proposed_player_behavior: A selected paid action reaches a real native item, skill/availability, body/source and local UI owner; unsupported bindings are reported to the author before release while runtime rechecks remain.

authoritative_owner.current: Engine registry/effect services and main native publication
authoritative_owner.proposed: Shared Engine supplies read-only binding/capability catalogue; authoring tooling consumes it; local integrator corrects definitions
authoritative_owner.boundary: No new effect or native state owner; foundations selects runtime semantics.

dependencies: Actual exported host capabilities and native ID catalogue
Typed per-effect reference descriptors, including outcomes/responses/ticks/enrollment
Existing campaign/mechanic IDs and status ledger

world_example.case: Short Measure inspection → funded wage/report → learned Load tally → actual later kit or stock effect
world_example.qualifier: Original held draft; current stock/travel/native UI gaps remain open.

acceptance_case.static: Deleting a declared source or native recipe binding produces a diagnostic at the authored effect path; JSON-valid unknown item is unresolved rather than marked functional. Context-dependent references remain explicitly late-bound.
acceptance_case.later_playable: A paid inspection binds employer stock and participants, publishes exactly one earned wage/item/source, and appears in its local native view; unsupported output rejects without spending.

findings.source_status: Current code evidence plus original workflow proposal. No new novel fact or universal superiority limit.
verification_limits: Read-only source tracing; no import or registry construction was executed here.
Reference closure cannot prove gameplay or dynamic predicate satisfaction.
findings.retain_or_simplify: Reuse item reconstruction, native unlock staging and the durable-before-publication host; add static closure around them.
findings.cheaper_alternative: An Engine-exported read-only descriptor of existing consumers suffices initially; do not instantiate native UI or author a parallel item system.

findings.title: Declare package activation and enrollment blast radius

evidence.claim: Common enrollment provisions all people except provision:false, creates all registered sites and schedules automatic events/controllers.
Several content families are manually composed into one shared simulation registry.
The held draft's two people explicitly use provision:false.
Explicit spawn requires an existing world and allocates a simulation actor/owner, including template controllers.
Explicit opening/enrollment/native publication remains Engine integration work.

findings.current_player_behavior: The current shared service enrollment deliberately provisions its configured services. Registering additional destination definitions changes that scan unless their activation fields and host policy say otherwise; import alone creates no live state.
findings.proposed_player_behavior: Register-only content stays dormant; explicit world/episode entry creates only the chosen supported actors, stock, sites/events and causes once. Intentionally common services remain available under a declared policy.

authoritative_owner.current: Shared Engine enrollment/spawn services and composed registry
authoritative_owner.proposed: Engine owns activation/instance contracts; each local integrator declares package activation; master selects entry policy
authoritative_owner.boundary: Authoring flags cannot allocate isolated native worlds or select a new origin/reset policy.

dependencies: Explicit activation policy for new packages
Declared initialization, automatic events and controller dependencies

world_example.world: Original Frontier and a proposed Mother of Learning destination
world_example.case: Opening Frontier work services must not silently create the destination's trainees or trial stock simply because their definitions were composed.
world_example.qualifier: Future destination activation example is original; no book-specific rule is asserted.

acceptance_case.static: Manifest lists register-only, explicit-start and intentionally common-enroll effects, people/sites/automatic checks. Omitted activation intent on a new package is reported, with current services grandfathered explicitly.
acceptance_case.later_playable: Frontier enrollment leaves the unchosen destination absent; chosen entry creates the declared state once and reentry retains it. An explicitly shared service is not suppressed accidentally.

findings.source_status: Verified enrollment source; cross-package consequence is a static integration risk, not a reproduced failure.
verification_limits: No new world was registered or enrolled.
All-site initialization and instance partition choices belong to foundations; no final record shape selected.
findings.retain_or_simplify: Retain explicit provision:false and existing opt-in wrappers. Prefer a lifecycle manifest over a second bootstrap engine.
findings.cheaper_alternative: Initially require an explicit activation declaration and composed closure review; use host-supported entry wrappers instead of a generic world-instantiation framework.

findings.title: Preserve compiler execution fields and project-local observations

evidence.claim: Compiler returns actorId/location/site/cost/effect fields but does not carry participant/target/co-location/role fields from phases; group and default UI section are field/workshop.
projectView reads field.project.<phase> observation facts without the project ID.
Executor supports role/target checks and explicit participant occupancy.
Saved jobs retain and validate participant reservations.
Current compiled workshop phases have one worker each.
Micro already asks for all-worker/tool/material reservations and actual project function.

findings.current_player_behavior: The current one-worker workshop compiles to ordinary commands with real costs, dependencies and claims. That example does not establish cooperative phases or project-neutral observed completion; silently added execution fields would not survive this compiler.
findings.proposed_player_behavior: A declared two-person construction phase reserves both actual workers and the relevant site/means. Multiple projects can reuse local phase names without sharing displayed progress or revealing unobserved world completion.

authoritative_owner.current: Engine site-project compiler and existing participant/knowledge services
authoritative_owner.proposed: Engine compiler writer plus local project integrator
authoritative_owner.boundary: Foundations chooses reservations/observation identity. This report reserves no code and creates no second project queue.

dependencies: Frozen supported phase schema and participant policy

world_example.case: Original workshop beam-fitting by player and craftsman, alongside a separate roof project with its own parts phase.
world_example.qualifier: Cooperative variant and roof are original proposals; current field workshop remains the baseline.

acceptance_case.static: A phase declaring participants/target/co-location either emits those fields faithfully or fails with its exact authored path. Two parts phases map to distinct observed-completion keys. Unsupported fields do not disappear silently.
acceptance_case.later_playable: A busy craftsman prevents beam-fitting; acceptance reserves both, cancellation follows the frozen cost policy, and the second project's People/Here view does not show the first project's completion.

findings.source_status: Verified compiler output omissions; missing generalization for selected future cooperative content, not a claim that current one-worker gameplay is broken.
verification_limits: No compiler or gameplay was executed.
A stable-ID/observation migration must be decided by Engine if saved meaning changes.
findings.retain_or_simplify: Keep compilation to existing commands/jobs/claims. Add only declared fields; do not spread arbitrary unvalidated input into runtime commands.
findings.cheaper_alternative: A fixed explicit two-worker command can qualify the native case before extending every project phase; retain the later reusable compiler gap.

findings.title: Show compiled control flow and external starts instead of assuming sequential scenes

evidence.claim: Ambient phases schedule a successor; offers schedule a successor on expiry. Responses retain their explicit effects.
Successful response applies its declared costs/effects and resolves the event; it does not execute the expiry list.
Road responses explicitly settle secured/detour while offer expiry leads to the later detour event.
Project prerequisites assume an externally started world fact.
Field content initializes related facts outside the compiler.

findings.current_player_behavior: The current road's successful response and unanswered expiry intentionally have different aftermath. Project/event helpers need authored external starts and facts; registry validity alone does not explain these edges to an author.
findings.proposed_player_behavior: Selected responses, refusal/delay and unanswered expiry produce their declared distinct aftermath; no automatic next step overwrites a successful solution or accepts work through a missed deadline.

authoritative_owner.current: Engine scene/project compilers and event response executor
authoritative_owner.proposed: Authoring compiler diagnostics expose flow; local scene writer chooses edges

world_example.case: Supply road support → secured; refuse → authored detour; leave unanswered → delayed association fallback.
world_example.qualifier: Current original road definition inspected; no fresh behavior proof.

acceptance_case.static: Generated graph shows response effects separately from expiry effects and marks external start dependencies unresolved until bound. Complex predicates remain opaque/unknown, with no fabricated reachability proof.
acceptance_case.later_playable: Supplying support retains secured aftermath; expiry takes fallback once; rendering a report causes no phase progression or obligation.

findings.source_status: Current code supports the asymmetry positively; flow graph and diagnostics are original authoring proposals.
verification_limits: General phase reachability and arbitrary fact-condition satisfiability were not established.
findings.retain_or_simplify: Retain explicit response/expiry branches. Do not make every response schedule the next phase automatically.
findings.cheaper_alternative: A static adjacency/entry table with authored predicates is sufficient; a graph editor or model checker is unnecessary for the first case.

findings.title: Use a small package descriptor and explicit view routing

evidence.claim: Top-level content manually imports independent action/source/definition exports.
Registry composition combines worlds, simulation, capabilities, sources and actions.
Every simulation family is currently assembled with explicit spread lists.
Generic panel excludes named groups and is gated to Village/Shack plus craftsman records.
Spawned people and role-target controls are also enumerated generically.
Pending-work attention routes through hardcoded group/panel choices.
Held content needs explicit family/source composition, local UI and exclusion from generic duplicate rows.

findings.current_player_behavior: Existing selected panels work through their own groups and native gates. New imported commands can remain inaccessible in Town, fall into generic attention routing or appear twice if a dedicated panel is added without coordinating generic enumeration.
findings.proposed_player_behavior: A package explicitly routes its actions, pending work, known people and quest projection into existing native Here/Practice/People consumers, with one action and attention target per declared route.

authoritative_owner.current: Engine composition/main/Notebook/UI owners; world modules own data
authoritative_owner.proposed: One shared Engine integration writer consumes a local package descriptor and renderer contract; world GM owns descriptor
authoritative_owner.boundary: Experience advises UI; renderer receives known read-only projections and does not grant enrollment/rewards.

world_example.case: Short Measure opens in Village and later Town square, with earned receiver report and accepted-work quest projection.
world_example.qualifier: Detached original draft; views/native integration unperformed.

acceptance_case.static: Composition report includes every declared family/source and detects duplicate IDs or omitted required family exports. Every player command and pending-work type has a declared consumer or deliberate hidden/unsupported reason.
acceptance_case.later_playable: A Town report is reachable through its local panel; generic craftsman/helper UI does not duplicate its actions or leak NPC logs; attention reaches its declared panel while preserving selected tabs.

findings.source_status: Current assembly/routing evidence; proposed descriptor is authoring structure, not an implemented plugin system.
verification_limits: Static declared routing does not prove mounting, focus or final player wording.
findings.retain_or_simplify: Keep JS data/factories emitting existing JSON definitions. Shared descriptor references existing renderer functions separately from serializable definitions.
findings.cheaper_alternative: Use one explicit composition helper/descriptor with opt-in family lists. Defer a general DSL, hot reload, schema editor and universal world template.

findings.title: Review source corrections separately from persistent content compatibility

evidence.claim: Templates, situation definitions and learned energy policies freeze in effect preparation.
Commands/jobs and encounter turns retain commitment data and definition revisions.
Loaded jobs/events/controllers still require registered IDs.
Ongoing controllers resolve current registered definitions.
Existing schema/native/save owners and durable publication remain authoritative.
Existing source-to-feature requirements include claim/locator/cutoff, original additions and actual function.
Naruto transfer penalties remain unresolved or original prototype choices; positive supported functions are preserved.

findings.current_player_behavior: Paid jobs and spawned bodies retain frozen data, but ID removal can reject saved state and current controller/power definitions may govern future behavior. A revised source note alone does not choose how old acquired means should change.
findings.proposed_player_behavior: Typo/attribution corrections leave paid work and earned means intact. Semantic content or source-rule corrections receive an explicit compatibility decision; unsupported assumptions stay visible rather than silently rewritten into canon.

authoritative_owner.current: Source dossier owners, local mechanic ledger and Shared Engine save/registry services
authoritative_owner.proposed: Source GM corrects claim; world integrator maps impacted mechanic IDs; Engine selects alias/migration/rejection; master approves scope
authoritative_owner.boundary: This audit selects no schema/migration/body penalty or save mutation.

dependencies: Stable required mechanic IDs already proposed in canonical plan

world_example.case: Frontier paid inspection survives a wording correction. A future eye-transfer penalty correction changes only the reviewed affected rule, not ancestry, donor identity or unrelated positive functions.
world_example.qualifier: Frontier case original; Naruto penalty remains U/O exactly as canonical plan states. No new canon fact.

acceptance_case.static: Change report classifies cosmetic/evidence/cutoff, future-definition behavior and persistent-ID/meaning changes; lists affected commitments/controllers/UI/required IDs. Removed ID without compatibility disposition remains unresolved.
acceptance_case.later_playable: After an allowed correction, frozen paid work keeps its documented settlement and one source receipt; changed future behavior follows the declared version policy without duplicate rewards or stripped unrelated faculties.

findings.source_status: Code compatibility evidence; source qualifiers are copied by reference to current owner, not relabelled as primary reading.
verification_limits: No source library/book was read or modified in this audit.
No migration/import/reload was run; version descriptors remain proposals.
findings.retain_or_simplify: Reference authoritative claim records and existing feature ledger rather than copy dossiers into every package or create a third ledger.
findings.cheaper_alternative: A small reviewed revision/impact table and explicit ID aliases may handle the first content correction; no automatic save-repair engine.

findings.title: Retain dynamic template-instance support and document the exact recipe

evidence.claim: Cause-based spawn identity, frozen template and ordered same-list aliases already exist.
Actual spawned actors have separate owners and template-attached controllers; native relocation is explicitly rejected.
Commands distinguish exact actor/target IDs from definition-role selectors.
Existing funded helper uses spawn alias, actorDefinitionId and targetDefinitionId.
Helper controller binds the reusable template role.

findings.current_player_behavior: The existing original helper can own inputs and execute role-bound commands under actual generated identity. Fixed cast content can use exact IDs. This already supplies a useful factory target, not proof of independent native world instances.
findings.proposed_player_behavior: More authored helpers use the same supported role recipe with independent actors, means and remembered aftermath, without copying the player/NPC inventory or leaking a transient alias into later commands.

authoritative_owner.current: Engine spawn/resolution/role services and local helper definitions
authoritative_owner.proposed: Local authoring recipe/factory writer; Shared Engine retains identity/native services
authoritative_owner.boundary: Foundation identity and world-instance semantics are retained, not redesigned by factories.

dependencies: Explicit definition ID versus actual actor ID roles
Namespaced immutable definitions and source-path metadata

world_example.case: Two original hired route carriers of one helper type each get one paid input, execute their own job and return their own output.
world_example.qualifier: Existing one-helper source support inspected; two-carrier example is an original future qualification.

acceptance_case.static: Recipe uses spawn before same-list aliases, role-based actor/target selectors and actual persisted target IDs for later calls. Native-bound spawn misuse receives an explicit capability diagnostic.
acceptance_case.later_playable: Both carriers retain separate stock/controllers/job outcomes across reload; duplicate/stale creation does not regrant supplies; collecting one output does not consume the other's.

findings.source_status: Positive current-code support; factory/recipe and multi-helper acceptance are original proposals.
verification_limits: No helpers were spawned or exercised.
A reusable person template does not establish arbitrary repeated sites, native NPC copies or multiverse histories.
findings.retain_or_simplify: Keep cause-based IDs, frozen templates, private owners and role selectors. Provide recipes and small parameterized JS factories before designing another lifecycle service.
findings.cheaper_alternative: Use the existing helper shape verbatim for the first new local role; generalize only the fields the second actual case needs.

findings.title: Give authors actionable diagnostics with explicit proof levels

evidence.claim: Validation throws messages and rejects unsafe/non-JSON data.
Registry validation is fail-fast by family/definition with useful existing invariants but no authored source-path diagnostic record.
Compiler checks IDs, dependency cycles and timing using error strings.
Scene checks timing/effects before generating events.
Historical successful registry construction still coexists with unqualified gameplay premises and no native/UI proof.

findings.current_player_behavior: Runtime rejects many invalid definitions safely. An author receives the first generic failure; repeated fixing can still leave contextual stock/travel or native-consumer gaps that a successful registry check does not reveal.
findings.proposed_player_behavior: Local content ships with fewer broken/missing controls because authors can locate the exact rule, dependency and proof gap before integration. Player-facing reasons use actual supported requirements, not diagnostic jargon.

authoritative_owner.proposed: Authoring preflight/report owner reuses validator contracts; local writers repair definitions; master keeps delivery status
authoritative_owner.boundary: Player UI copy and behavior acceptance remain experience/Engine gates.

world_example.case: A compiler-generated workshop command reports the offending project/phase/effect path; Short Measure stays detached despite its historical registry receipt.
world_example.qualifier: Diagnostic and status workflow original; held receipt is historical.

acceptance_case.static: Diagnostic includes code/severity, package/feature ID, family/definition ID, authored field path, reference and remediation owner. Independent errors aggregate deterministically; dependent checks stop after invalid shape. Contextual claims are unresolved until operational evidence exists.
acceptance_case.later_playable: Local controls display correct ordinary eligibility reasons and selected actions pass the permitted journey/retention gate; source/publication safeguards remain active.

findings.source_status: Current fail-fast source evidence; structured diagnostics and proof-level output are proposals.
verification_limits: No diagnostic tool was implemented or benchmarked.
No reduction in tokens, authoring time or runtime cost measured; file/word counts would be surrogates only.
findings.retain_or_simplify: Reuse validation rules and keep assertions at runtime. Diagnostics wrap or share those rules, rather than fork a second acceptance vocabulary.
findings.cheaper_alternative: A deterministic CLI/JSON link report suffices initially; editor integrations and automated gameplay generation are deferred.
